findings.summary: The hand-built `HEAD:.ai-sdlc/reviews/${f}` path was rewritten as `['.ai-sdlc','reviews',f].join('/')`. This dodges the new lint regex without using the single path helper, which goes against the task's intent of one source of truth. It is behaviourally safe here, because `f` is a real directory entry and must not be lowercased. A cleaner fix would be to give `reviews-ledger.ts` a helper that takes a file name, or to use `reviewsLedgerRelativePath(taskId)` when the task id is known.

findings.summary: The HANDBUILT regex only flags the literal followed by `${` or a quote and `+`. AC3 says to fail on any `.ai-sdlc/reviews/` literal in non-test source. A path built by other means, such as a `path.join('.ai-sdlc/reviews', id)` call or a literal ending in `/` that is then concatenated, would not be caught. The detector test also covers only one positive and one negative case.

findings.summary: The `['.ai-sdlc','reviews',f].join('/')` form avoids the lint gate rather than using the helper. It is a hand-built ledger path in disguise, and the gate cannot see it. Here `f` is a directory-listing filename, so it may not be a task id and the lowercasing helper may not apply. It is worth a comment saying so.
